reviews.review: The best Aliens game since Isolation. I love playing both of them in VR with mods! The Lore and level design in this game are amazing! All the weapons are fun to use and the Xenos are relentless!
Very cool and well-made, with lots of classes, guns, and customization options, but a bit harder than it needed to be… kinda a skill issue tho :3

Matchmaking is dead, even with cross-platform matchmaking. You're literally better off playing ANYTHING else. I'm currently getting a refund. I was so excited for this game just to be swiftly disapointed. Once again no good Alien game for the foreseeable future.

[h1] As a close friend of mine put it: “I feel really offended by this. I'm about to cry, and not because of joy.” [/h1] 

[h3] I was the one who gifted it to him for Christmas, hoping to spend some time together and take a break from the same old videogames that had been monopolizing my empty and questionable days. [/h3] 

We have always been huge fans of the franchise and, unlike the so-called “critics,” we loved AVP because it managed to make us feel emotions by letting us experience the Alien and Predator universe firsthand.

[b] I only have these four negative points to mention: [/b]

1. This game is boringly repetitive and feels like something straight out of old arcade cabinets. 
2. The graphics are nice and relatively well done, perfect for a game meant to be played in first person… unfortunately, as a TPS it doesn’t work and never will. It completely kills immersion in what could have been a game with real potential, now totally wasted.
3. There are no cutscenes, the gameplay is identical across all levels (which are literally just 3 levels reused across 4 campaigns plus 1 DLC), for a total of 12 levels with an average duration of about 15 minutes each, bringing the ENTIRE campaign to just 3 hours.
4. There are no real rewards at the end of each campaign, and this—purely my opinion—leaves a very bitter taste. 

Sure, these levels were designed to be replayed over and over again… [b]but for what purpose? [/b] To level up weapons and characters? To complete “daily missions”? [b]But why?[/b] At that point, why not add a season pass too? [u]At least there would have been a reason to cash in on it and make it a knowingly crappy game.[/u]

[h2]Instead, NO.[/h2]
[h3] [i]I honestly don’t understand how this game is reviewed so positively. [/i] [/h3]
[u] Marketed as the best in the series, I buy it for myself and my friend, I fill myself with hope, I DELUDE myself, and then I’m left deeply disappointed.[/u] 

[h3] [b]It left a bitter taste in my mouth, disappointment in my soul, and depressed me to the point of ruining my last day of vacation before going back to work.[/b] [/h3]

[h1] I feel really offended by this.  I'm about to cry, and not because of joy. [/h1]

[hr][/hr]

Let's start from the premise that [b]I am a huge fan of the Alien franchise since I was little, and well, of Predator too.[/b]
A dear friend of mine gifted me this game, complete with DLC, so we played it together.

At first glance, the premise seemed cool, we were super hyped and couldn't wait to progress.
The first level was pretty simple and straightforward, but that's normal in any game; after all, the controls and mechanics need to be taught.
Then came the second level, and it was identical.
So was the third.
And the fourth.
And the fifth.
[b]Until we got to the last mission of the main game. SPOILER ALERT: a total flop.[/b]

Maybe trying the DLC would be a better idea!
[i]Turns out, no. It wasn't.[/i]
Same stuff, just different models.

[hr][/hr]

The graphics are nice, the lore is kind of accurate.

But...

[list]
[*]No cutscenes (the only one there is lasts about 10 seconds and is meaningless).
[*]IDENTICAL gameplay with no sight of variation.
[*]Enemies are almost ONLY RESKINNED AND BUFFED.
[*]Bugs everywhere (we had to restart several missions because Xenos were stuck in the walls, preventing us from completing the objective).
[*]Third-person view totally reduces immersion and scare factor.
[/list]

[hr][/hr]

Unfortunately, I have to say with a heavy heart that it's truly an insult to everything that is the world and lore of Alien.
[b] I am deeply offended. [/b] 

Alien should be a game made of anxiety, not a point-and-click zombie wave shooter. I understand the target audience, making it similar to an arcade game.

There doesn't seem to be the slightest bit of love behind this game. It really struck me as a way to lure fans in with a shiny object, in order to cover up an old failure.

[b]I hate giving negative reviews, but this one game really hit me hard and caused me constant stress.[/b]
There was not the slightest reward after every action performed.
[h3]The feeling was that of having a job where you do the exact same thing for the rest of your life, just waiting for the day to end, but knowing that soon you will have to start the day again doing the exact same thing, until the end.[/h3]

[hr][/hr]

[h2]AVP, I miss you.[/h2]
[h2]Isolation, you too.[/h2]
